page: Microsoft Azure L16as_v3 is a storage and memory-focused virtual machine belonging to the LASv3 family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with an x86_64 architecture, featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz and includes a 32 MB L3 cache. This instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, and includes 4004 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capabilities.

Benchmark data reveals a mixture of strong single-core capabilities and moderate memory throughput constraints. The server achieves strong performance in stress-ng single-core CPU testing and small-model LLM text generation. However, a notable hardware tradeoff is present in its memory subsystem: while cached small-block read bandwidth is average, uncached large-block read and write memory bandwidths fall into the bottom 25% of tested systems. Multi-core CPU performance, database operations, and web serving throughput remain consistently in the average tier.

Given the inclusion of 4004 GB of local storage alongside 128.0 GB of RAM, the L16as_v3 offers high resource density for data-intensive applications without requiring external storage attachments. This configuration is highly suitable for relational databases, NoSQL stores, caching layers, and data-intensive workloads that require a balance of high-capacity local storage and substantial memory capacity.
